text:
ana: Anyone else seeing token/sec drop after the main merge? Canary in us-east-1 showed ~28% token/sec decrease around 02:10 UTC.

mike: Yup. Alerts from the canary perf probe. CI perf job flagged p99 latency up and tokens/sec sag for ctb. Rolled the canary back to previous kernel policy but still saw a drop during the window.

sri: I'm starting a bisect across the last 5 commits. First suspect is the kernel-selection heuristic tweak in commit 0f9b7e0 that biases short sequences toward memcpy.

julia: Can you paste the profiler snapshot from the canary? :eyes:

ana: (typo: meant ana) Sending initial flame excerpt from 02:12. Observed: big increase in memcpy time on dispatch thread and KV cache hitrate fell ~4%. Excerpt below.

ana: ```
pprof summary (canary 02:12):
 60.1% runtime::dispatch_memcpy
 18.4% kernel::attention_kernel_select
 12.3% kv::lookup_miss_path
  6.2% coalescer::drain_wait
  3.0% other
```

mike: Interesting — kv hit drop + memcpy increase suggests coalescing/kvcache interaction. The scheduler prefetch change landed in the same release; it may be evicting prefixes earlier and causing more full-input memcpys.

sri: Bisect update: enabling the adaptive prefetch window (scheduler: prefetch-window-adaptive) reproduces the token/sec sag in a local canary. Reverting the commit locally restores tokens/sec to baseline.

julia: Can you share the kernel-routing logs around the spike? Need to see if we're falling back to memcpy more often.

mike: Kernel routing snippet: ```
[02:11:58] route: batch_id=3423 seq=3 chosen_kernel=fused_copy
[02:12:01] route: batch_id=3426 seq=4 chosen_kernel=memcpy (fallback) reason=kv_miss
[02:12:03] route: batch_id=3430 seq=2 chosen_kernel=memcpy reason=insufficient_coalesce
```

mike: Looks like prefetch change reduces coalescing, creating more tiny microbatches that pick memcpy path.

julia: Proposal: hold rollout, revert adaptive prefetch, add KV lifetime guard to avoid premature eviction. We can reintroduce adaptive prefetch with adjusted thresholds after more metrics.

max: I'll open a revert PR (revert: scheduler adaptive prefetch) and run the canary + perf CI. @perf-bot kick off perf_job/ctb-canary.

perf-bot: Perf CI queued: https://ci.redwood/rs/345/perf/ctb-canary-345999 (ETA ~15m).

ana: Also seeing repeated "coalescer: wait_for_batch" spikes aligned with queue depth oscillations. Could be interplay: prefetch triggers evictions -> lower kvcache hits -> increased memcpy -> coalescer sees more small batches -> more wait churn.

sri: I'll add extra instrumentation: coalescer wake timers + kvcache eviction traces. If prefetch reduces prefix retention, we'll catch it in the eviction trace.

mike: If CI perf passes with revert + kv-guard, we can accept the revert and iterate on prefetch config. Need to ensure kernel-selection doesn't over-index to memcpy for borderline seq lengths.

julia: Putting rollout ON_HOLD for main until canary stabilizes. Ping infra for manual canary throttling if needed.

perf-bot: Perf CI completed: ctb-canary-345999 -> baseline tokens/sec restored, p99 down to expected range. Regression resolved with revert. Details: https://ci.redwood/rs/345/perf/results/345999

ana: Great. Thanks all — follow-ups: (1) merge revert PR, (2) add KV lifetime guard + stronger coalescer wake metrics, (3) run targeted kernel-selection A/B to validate fallback thresholds.

julia: I'll file follow-up tickets and schedule a short postmortem doc. Leaving rollout hold until next canary validates the fixes.

max: PR opened: revert/0f9b7e0 + kv-guard branch. Running canary now.

sri: Adding instrumentation ticket: ENG-ctb-evict-trace. Will post traces in this thread once available.

julia: Thanks team. We'll regroup after the updated canary. :thumbsup:
